highlightAliases.old: HD-IIV4 (high-dose) has 4× the antigen dose of standard-dose vaccine and is more effective in older adults; aIIV4 (MF59-adjuvanted) also shows increased immunogenicity and is linked in observational studies to reduced hospitalization for flu, pneumonia, and cardiovascular events; RIV4 (recombinant) also promising. ACIP endorses any of these for older adults (p1735).
highlightAliases.new: The edition’s HD-IIV4 (high-dose) has 4× the antigen dose of standard-dose vaccine and is more effective in older adults; aIIV4 (MF59-adjuvanted) also shows increased immunogenicity and is linked in observational studies to reduced hospitalization for flu, pneumonia, and cardiovascular events; RIV4 (recombinant) also promising. Current US ACIP guidance preferentially recommends age-appropriate high-dose, adjuvanted, or recombinant influenza vaccine for adults 65 or older; the seasonal formulations are now trivalent (p1735).
Peramivir (IV) — first FDA-approved in December 2014, IV-only formulation (p1736; FDA original approval, application 206426).

highlightAliases.old: Asymptomatic/presymptomatic transmission was estimated in one study to account for up to 79% of documented cases (p1738).
highlightAliases.new: An early model attributed 79% of documented cases to people whose infections were undocumented; undocumented infection could include mild symptoms (p1738).

highlightAliases.old: Vaccine candidates demonstrated >90% effectiveness against infection (p1740).
highlightAliases.new: The original randomized mRNA vaccine trials demonstrated over 90% efficacy against symptomatic COVID-19; preventing all infections was a different endpoint (p1740; Polack et al., 2020, and Baden et al., 2021).
